subject: Post-demo: Performance checks & SLO fitment for OmniCard (dedicated)
messages:
From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ramirez <alex@omnicard.ai>, Sam Lee <sam.lee@omnicard.ai>
Cc: evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-02T13:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: Performance checks & SLO fitment for OmniCard (dedicated)

Hi Alex / Sam —

Thanks again for the demo time today. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source for the performance conversation and Dedicated sizing validation. I captured numbers from the call; please correct anything I misunderstood.

Customer targets & workload we heard today:
- Primary path: streaming multi-turn assistant for card auth flows (short prompts, avg 120 tokens per turn).
- Streaming concurrency target: 75 concurrent live sessions (concurrent clients with an active stream).
- Average steady token rate per stream: ~20 tokens/s; bursts to 120 tokens/s for short spikes.
- Batch/async inference: up to 25 concurrent batch requests at peak, avg 512 tokens per request (non-streaming).
- SLOs you want validated: first-token latency p95 <= 350ms (end-to-end), steady-state token p95 <= 90ms, and availability 99.9% for the Dedicated pool.

Redwood preliminary capacity ask (to validate):
- Sustained throughput to size: ~12k tokens/sec combined (streaming steady-state + batch).
- Starting validation configurations: H100 narrow-precision profile (2 nodes), A100 cost-first profile (4 nodes), and a mixed-setup for fallback (2xA100 + 1xH100).

Proposed validation plan (high-level):
1) Microbench: kernel selection + token-latency matrix on each GPU type (we’ll run the matrix in the attachment).
2) End-to-end pilot: 48-hour replay with your anonymized traffic_profile_omnicard.jsonl + synthetic burst windows.
3) Acceptance criteria: first-token p95 <= 350ms, steady-state token p95 <= 90ms, sustained throughput >= 12k t/s for >= 95% of 48h window, CPU + GPU utilization below our operational guardrails.

Next steps / asks for OmniCard:
- Please share a 24–72h sample of production trace (anonymized) and an API key for the pilot harness (we provided a share link below).
- Confirm which region you want Dedicated in (we assume us-west-2 unless you say otherwise).
- Let us know procurement cadence — if you expect to sign a reservation after the pilot, we can pre-configure capacity for drop-in.

I attached the SLO validation template and the GPU latency matrix we’ll fill out during microbench. Marcus will own the kernel/run configs; Evelyn will run the orchestration and report.

If that looks right, I’ll schedule the microbench for next Tuesday and send over the pilot start checklist.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Solutions 
Redwood Inference

Attachments: slo_validation_plan.csv (template), gpu_latency_matrix.xlsx (matrix), traffic_profile_omnicard.jsonl (placeholder)
From: Alex Ramirez <alex@omnicard.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Lee <sam.lee@omnicard.ai>, Procurement <procure@omnicard.ai>
Date: 2027-10-02T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance checks & SLO fitment for OmniCard (dedicated)

Jonas —

Thanks for the crisp recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- The 75 concurrent streams number is conservative; our Q4 target could push to 120 for short windows. Can you show headroom?
- The critical thing for us is first-token latency for the auth acceptance step (this triggers the mobile UI). If steady-state token latency is worse but first-token is in bounds, we can tolerate some variance.
- We can provide a 72h anonymized trace by Monday. Procurement asked to see the pilot cost estimate and a sample SOW for Dedicated setup — can you attach a rough one?

On GPUs: our infra team prefers A100 for cost predictability but they'd accept H100 for initial pilot if you can demonstrate a clear p95 improvement.

Thanks,
Alex Ramirez
Head of Platform
OmniCard

PS — Sam will be the technical lead and will coordinate the trace and procurement contact info.
From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ramirez <alex@omnicard.ai>, Sam Lee <sam.lee@omnicard.ai>
Cc: evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-03T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance checks & SLO fitment for OmniCard (dedicated)

Appreciate the clarifications, Alex — that helps. Quick responses and an updated plan below.

1) Headroom and spike handling
- We’ll run the microbench with short spike profiles (120 concurrent streams for 2–5 minute windows) to measure headroom.
- Our recommendation: pilot with 2xH100 to validate lowest possible first-token latency, with an A100 cluster standing by as the cost-efficient target for the reservation. If the H100 pilot shows >40% p95 improvement in first-token latency vs A100 for your exact prompts, we’ll recommend H100 reservation; otherwise A100 reserve with an H100 fallback pool.

2) Sizing math (simple):
- Streaming steady: 75 streams * 20 t/s = 1,500 t/s.
- Batch peak: 25 RPS * 512 tokens = 12,800 t/s.
- Combined peak: ~14.3k t/s.
- We’ll size reserve to sustain 12k t/s (operational headroom + autoscale available for short spikes).

3) Acceptance criteria (refined):
- First-token end-to-end p95 <= 350ms AND p99 <= 650ms during pilot windows.
- Steady-state token p95 <= 90ms.
- No more than 1 minute cumulative unavailability per 24h (target 99.995% in pilot).

4) Deliverables we’ll provide before pilot
- Pilot SOW (rough) and a conservative pilot cost estimate for both H100- and A100-based configs.
- Completed microbench results (kernel/sequence-length matrix) and a filled gpu_latency_matrix.xlsx.
- A playbook for fallback routing and cache priming so your mobile team does not see cold-first-token spikes.

Marcus: can you confirm the exact microbench config we should run (seq length buckets, batching configs, quantization levels)? I’ll start the SOW draft and attach it to the pilot link.

Alex / Sam: send the 72h trace link and confirm region (us-west-2). Also please tell procurement who should receive the SOW (email) and confirm any SOC2 / compliance checkpoints we should include.

Thanks — I’ll queue the microbench as soon as Marcus confirms.

—Jonas

Attachments: pilot_sow_draft.pdf (coming), cost_estimate_pilot.xlsx (coming)
From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Alex Ramirez <alex@omnicard.ai>, Sam Lee <sam.lee@omnicard.ai>
Cc: evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-04T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance checks & SLO fitment for OmniCard (dedicated)

Quick tech notes and confirm the microbench matrix I’ll run.

Planned microbench matrix (I/O):
- Sequence length buckets: 32, 128, 256, 512, 1024.
- Batch sizes: 1, 4, 8, 16 for non-streaming; continuous token emission for streaming tests.
- Quantization profiles: fp16, int8 (where supported), and an 8-bit safe path.
- Metrics captured: first-token latency, per-token steady-state latency, GPU util, CPU util, NVLink bandwidth, memory footprint, and 95/99 percentiles for each bucket.

Acceptance automation & test harness:
- I’ll push the configs and runner to the pilot harness: https://redwood-internal/share/omnicard/pilot-harness (you should have reader access).
- Test cases I want from OmniCard: 1) short auth flow (avg 120 tokens), 2) long policy retrieval (avg 702 tokens), 3) burst window profile (120 concurrent streams for 3 minutes). The 72h trace will let us derive realistic arrival distributions.

Expected outputs after microbench (deliverables):
- Filled gpu_latency_matrix.xlsx with p50/p95/p99 numbers per GPU per seq-length.
- Recommended reserved pool (H100 vs A100 count) with expected cost delta and expected p95 improvements.
- A pilot-run dashboard link and a short runbook for your ops team.

Action owners & timeline
- Alex / Sam: provide 72h trace and confirm procurement recipient (by Mon 2027-10-04).
- Jonas: SOW + cost estimate (EOD 2027-10-04).
- Marcus: run microbench (2027-10-05 through 2027-10-06) and deliver matrix.
- Evelyn: schedule pilot and run orchestration (once microbench is complete).

If everyone is aligned I’ll start the microbench tomorrow morning.

—Marcus Lin
Senior Performance Engineer
Redwood Inference
